nodes.label: Secrets CLI direction — the six decisions (D1-D6), including DROP FNOX (grilling outcome, 2026-08-04)
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: STATUS: the fnox / Doppler / keychain secrets arrangement is DECIDED-TO-BE-REPLACED, NOT YET BUILT. 'This is a planning artifact.' No code ships from it — the existing runbook for how to add/declare a secret via fnox is what still runs today.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The north star, in Ray's words: 'Dev projects on the mac having a universal way to crud api keys secrets.' Replaces 'takeover'; reconcile, scoping and CRUD ownership all serve it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D1 (Settled) — Scoping = additive declaration + reconcile: a project declares what it additionally needs; the CLI checks the declaration against reality. Scoping buys zero confinement, accepted because confinement is already dead as a goal.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D2 (Superseded, VOIDED BY D5) — Declarations were going to use fnox's native hierarchy (committed fnox.toml + gitignored fnox.local.toml); that mechanism leaves with fnox. Its intent survives — a project declares what it needs and reconcile reports drift — new home is `doppler setup --scope`. Re-decide in /to-spec.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D3 (Settled) — Storage is the status quo: Keychain holds exactly DOPPLER_TOKEN; Doppler CLI owns CRUD for secrets; the other 49 stay Doppler-sourced.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D4 (Settled) — The highest-value verbs for secrets are rotate / classify / retire, not create.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D5 (Settled, RESOLVED 2026-08-04) — DROP FNOX. The secrets stack becomes Doppler + macOS keychain. Was 'fnox stays (PROVISIONAL)'; reversed on measurement rather than argument.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D6 (Open, near-zero variance) — Language deferred, and largely pre-decided: Rust's only genuine win is typed in-process fnox-core, which is read-only; D5 removed fnox, so that argument is now moot entirely.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The original, struck-through D5 verdict: 'fnox stays' — PROVISIONAL. Reversed by the resolved D5 in §6, on measurement rather than argument.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: CORRECTED finding for D1: 'fnox has no subtraction primitive' is WRONG as originally stated. /prototype claim 2 measured the opposite against a fixture with a real declared profile: `-P shell --no-defaults` yields exactly the profile's 2 secrets out of 52. fnox's subtraction primitive exists; it is profile-selected, not directory-selected — the six no-profile arms could only show the degenerate 0/50-51 split.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A project declaration silently OVERRIDES the global entry of the same name — 49 global + 1 local on collision vs 50 + 1 on the control, rc=0, stderr 0 bytes. No override-warning setting exists anywhere; introspection is after-the-fact only (`fnox config-files`, `fnox list --sources`).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `fnox sync -p keychain` cannot be built: sync re-encrypts with a local encryption provider and writes a `sync` field into the TOML, not into a keystore; Keychain declares only RemoteStorage, no encrypt(). Doppler cannot address a laptop keystore either — writing all 50 secrets directly to the keychain was rejected on cost (50 keychain reads per prompt, 50 ACL grants per fnox bump) for ~no secrecy gain, since all 50 already live in every process under `env = true`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: fnox's unique feature — an automatic chpwd/precmd hook — is inert on this Mac: zero project fnox.toml files exist in dotfiles or knowledge-base, the only one (mde's) declares no secrets, and `~/.doppler/.doppler.yaml` holds exactly one scope, '/'. Doppler CLI v3.76.1 already natively provides CRUD, --scope, an encrypted offline cache, doppler run, and shell-eval-able env.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Rust buys read-only access only: `fnox-core` is rlib/Rust-only (no [lib] section, zero cdylib/wasm-bindgen/napi/pyo3 hits); the public Fnox API has get/list but no `set` — writes live in the binary's unpublished commands module. `fnox mcp` offers strictly fewer verbs than shelling out. `usage`, the jdx CLI generator, works fine for a non-Rust CLI.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Consumption sweep across 28 repos, 162 .mcp.json files, ~/.claude.json, ~/.config/: CONSUMED 25 · AMBIENT 4 · ALIAS 4 · ORPHAN 17.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Rotate evidence: one GitHub PAT lives under four names, not aliases — mise documents a precedence chain (MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN → GITHUB_API_TOKEN → GITHUB_TOKEN) plus GITHUB_MCP_PAT. There is no documented rotate procedure; a running fnox daemon serves the rotated-away value until idle timeout.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Classify evidence: 19 of 50 secrets are not secrets (regions, buckets, endpoints, protocols, usernames, handles, client IDs, booleans). secrets-out-of-the-shell-env.md rule 3 forbids value-based redaction for this reason — a short or empty 'secret' corrupts every log the tool writes.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Retire evidence: 17 orphans, 14 from one dead project (an S3-backed Grafana/Loki/Mimir/Tempo/OpenLIT stack plus a NextAuth app). There is no documented delete procedure, and fnox is CRU only — the Provider trait has no delete method at all.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: By contrast, create is already a documented 9-step runbook across four systems (docs/secrets-doppler-fnox-keychain.md:347-397), of which mde-secret-add already automates steps 3-7, everything except doctor.toml.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: One design already refuted before being built: only 1 of 50 secrets is interpolated into an MCP config via ${VAR}; the other 49 arrive by environment inheritance. A reconcile code-scan that greps for ${VAR} would report ~49 false orphans — the project-scope/code seam needs a different mechanism than the spec assumed.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Refuted belief: 'MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN and GITHUB_API_TOKEN are aliases of GITHUB_TOKEN' is wrong as stated — the consumption agent found they are three distinct variables in a documented precedence chain.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: What /prototype must settle: (1) does `mise bootstrap dotfiles` status --json --missing really exit 1 on missing/differs/source-gone; (2) fnox export against a real declared profile (zero [profiles.*] exist today); (3) the cleartext-write defect in `fnox set ... --provider doppler`; (4) fnox-full vs fnox-less timing, and whether the DOPPLER_TOKEN keychain-ACL story survives without fnox. 'This decides D5, and D6 follows.'
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: What /prototype measured: every terminal still gets its secrets fnox-less — 49 of 50 in a clean shell, 0.117s offline (the 50th is DOPPLER_TOKEN itself, from the keychain); fnox hook-env costs ~0.009s on every prompt vs fnox-less ~0.117s once per shell; the keychain ACL is a one-time, automatable approval at creation only (an ACL trusting only the fnox binary TIMEOUTs at 8s behind a GUI dialog); an existing ACL cannot be amended non-interactively, so migration is delete-and-recreate; `doppler setup --scope` is genuinely directory-bound; `doppler setup` does not persist the token.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Durability axis, favoring D5: `-T` binds a binary PATH; fnox's is version-pinned (five versions on disk since April) so its ACL breaks on every upgrade. /usr/bin/security is OS-stable — an ACL granted to it never breaks.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Scoping axis, favoring D5: `doppler setup --scope` is directory-bound. fnox's [profiles.*] subtraction is real (measured: -P shell --no-defaults -> exactly 2 of 52) but profile-selected, not directory-selected, and zero profiles are declared on this host.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Simplicity axis, favoring D5: four moving parts (Doppler + fnox + age + keychain) become two; the CLI's write path drops from 4 systems to 2, which was most of its complexity.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Churn axis, favoring D5: the 49-ciphertext re-encrypt on every add/remove disappears with the age cache; Doppler's --fallback is per-fetch instead.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: What is given up, stated plainly: 22 unused providers; the age `sync` cache (replaced by Doppler --fallback); and profile subtraction. The CLI, not fnox, now owns local-cache correctness.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Migration carried forward: delete-and-recreate the mde-fnox DOPPLER_TOKEN keychain item with -T /usr/bin/security, plus a `doppler setup --scope` per project — both scripted, no password prompts. Register scopes with RESOLVED paths: macOS /var is a symlink to /private/var, and an unresolved scope silently never matches.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Upstream defect to report (claim 3): `fnox set --provider doppler` returns rc=0 and writes the plaintext value into the config rather than writing through or refusing. Control arm `age` writes ciphertext. jdx/fnox has Issues disabled, so this needs a PR or discussion.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: D1's stated reason was too strong, corrected: fnox does have a subtraction primitive; it is profile-selected, not directory-selected. The decision (D1) stands; only the justification is corrected.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `mise bootstrap dotfiles` confirmed usable (claim 1): symlink-each applies and `status --json --missing` exits 1 on missing, differs, dangling-symlink, and source-dir-gone.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Probe corrections recorded in §5 as reusable traps: a path-spelling bound produced a false negative (grep vs fnox's own './' in the printed source column); a probe aimed at a directory with no fnox tree in it; agents self-caught three bugs (a lockfile awk printing only the first major, `gh repo list --limit 200` masking a true 623, a crates.io sweep with a broken parser and no control arm); and the consumption agent refuted the GITHUB_TOKEN-alias belief it was handed.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Probe discipline in §6: five broken probes, all caught by their own controls — a path-spelling bound (recurrence of the same trap); a probe aimed at a directory with no source; a [dotfiles] fixture whose keys mise rejected, making every arm return rc=0; a claim-3 control (`plain`) that is itself a cleartext store, discriminating nothing; and `zsh -f` inheriting the environment (a do-nothing control reported 47 of 50 set) plus a `doppler secrets --only-names` parse bug reporting 0 names against a real 49.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Item 19: nothing verifies the proxy end-to-end — header substitution into authorization, allowed vs rejected destinations, and the ephemeral CA path are unverified. Non-blocking, phase 3.

hyperedges.label: The no-code banner scopes all six decisions: DECIDED, NOT BUILT — this is a planning artifact and no code ships from it.
D5's resolution to drop fnox cascades through the other decisions: it voids D2's fnox-hierarchy mechanism, moots D6's Rust argument, and reverses the earlier 'fnox stays' provisional ruling.
The four /prototype claims (mise bootstrap fixture, real fnox profile export, cleartext-write defect, fnox-full vs fnox-less timing) together resolved D5 and, following from it, D6.
The north star — a universal way to CRUD api keys/secrets on the Mac — governs scoping (D1), storage/CRUD ownership (D3), and D5's simplification down to Doppler + Keychain.
